name: at-most-once drops duplicate identities immediately
test:
handler = MessageHandler(0, 2, [(0, 1)], 'at-most-once')
message = Message('hello', 1, 0, 1, [])
handler.receive(message); handler.receive(message)
assert [item.content for item in handler.get_delivered()] == ['hello']

name: at-least-once buffers a sequence gap and requests it once
test:
requests = []
handler = MessageHandler(0, 2, [(0, 1)], 'at-least-once', lambda sender, seq: requests.append((sender, seq)))
handler.receive(Message('second', 1, 1, 2, [])); handler.receive(Message('second-again', 1, 1, 3, []))
assert requests == [(1, 0)]
handler.receive(Message('first', 1, 0, 1, []))
assert [item.content for item in handler.get_delivered()] == ['first', 'second']

name: exactly-once releases causal dependents after their prerequisite arrives
test:
requests = []
handler = MessageHandler(2, 3, [(0, 1), (1, 2)], 'exactly-once', lambda sender, seq: requests.append((sender, seq)))
handler.receive(Message('world', 1, 0, 2, [(0, 0)]))
handler.receive(Message('world duplicate', 1, 0, 3, [(0, 0)]))
assert requests == [(0, 0)]
handler.receive(Message('hello', 0, 0, 1, []))
assert [item.content for item in handler.get_delivered()] == ['hello', 'world']
